commit_message:
[Codegen] Add VectorDistribute constraints for attention

Adds emitVectorDistributeAttentionConstraintsForOp +
buildVectorDistributeAttentionKnobsDict next to the existing
contraction/conv VectorDistribute versions in
LLVMGPUConstraintGenerator, and refactors emitVectorDistributeConstraintsForOp
to branch by op kind so OnlineAttentionOp routes through the new
emitter. emitMMALookup gains an `mmaIdxKnobName` parameter so the two
attention matmuls (QK and PV) carry distinct knobs without colliding
on "mma_idx", and returns the index knob alongside the shape lookups
so layout-binding can reuse it without redeclaring KnobOps.

Knob template (top-level) matches native attention codegen output
(KernelConfig.cpp's setAttention…):
  workgroup          ([1 at batch dims, m_tile on innermost M,
                       n_tile on innermost N])
  reduction          (red_k2 on innermost K2)
  promote_operands   ([0, 1, 2]) + promotion_types
                     ([derived_thread_config]*3)
  decomposition_config
    qk_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
    pv_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
  workgroup_size     ([wg_size_x, 1, 1])
  subgroup_size      (sg_size)

Per-matmul `lowering_config` entries are typed
`IREE::GPU::LoweringConfigAttr`s (not raw DictAttrs — attention
codegen casts them to LoweringConfigAttr, so a raw dict gets silently
rejected and codegen falls back to default per-matmul behavior).
Each carries mma_kind (one_of_knob<qk_mma_idx>/<pv_mma_idx>),
promote_operands + promotion_types (fixed [0,1]/[1] with
derived_thread_config), and subgroup_basis whose counts reference
the top-level sg_m_cnt / sg_n_cnt knobs at the M / N dim positions
(mapping projected per matmul: drop N for QK, drop K1 for PV).

In addition to the per-matmul lowering_config knobs above, the
template declares three SMT-only auxiliary sub-dictionaries that
codegen never reads (the materializer skips them; the verifier
whitelists them):
  smt_internal_subgroup_tile_counts — sg_m_tcnt / sg_n_tcnt / sg_k_tcnt
    factorize m_tile / n_tile / red_k2 into
    (subgroup_count × subgroup_tile_count × intrinsic_size) so the
    schedule-validity helper can reason about each factor.
  smt_internal_mma_layouts — 4 × 6 MMASingleSubgroupLayout fields
    (qk_acc / pv_lhs / pv_rhs / pv_acc each carrying element_x/y,
    thread_x/y, tstrides_x/y) bound to the chosen MMA via
    iree_codegen.smt.lookup ops over qk_mma_idx / pv_mma_idx.
  smt_internal_bools — use_col_major and
    can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input, encoded as int_knob ∈ {0, 1}
    (BoolKnobAttr doesn't exist yet); each constrained equivalent to
    a match_layout disjunction over the layout fields above.

Three pieces of generic infrastructure had to learn about typed
wrapper attrs to keep this end-to-end:

1. `hasKnobName` (ConstraintsOp::verify) rewritten with
   AttrTypeWalker so the verifier sees knob references nested inside
   any typed attribute, not just DictionaryAttr/ArrayAttr.

2. `materializeKnobAttribute` (MaterializeSMTConstraintAssignments)
   gains a LoweringConfigAttr case that recurses into the inner
   DictAttr and re-wraps the materialized result.

3. `extractKnobValue` (VerifyPipelineConstraints) gains a
   LoweringConfigAttr case + a generic Attribute-equality `Default`
   for fixed typed leaves like `#iree_gpu.derived_thread_config` in
   per-matmul promotion_types lists. `extractKnobValues` now
   distinguishes intentionally-absent SMT-only auxiliary keys (the
   three `smt_internal_*` sub-dicts) from real config drift: missing
   non-aux entries now fail verification instead of silently
   skipping every constraint that referenced them.

Constraint body ports `generate_attention_vector_distribute_constraints`
(sharktuner/dispatch_constraints.py:434-596) 1:1 — bijective parity
vs the legacy Python tuner is the gate (110 = 110 on the parity
fixture; see the parity-proof snapshots on the tuner side). The body
covers:
  - sg_size == preferred_subgroup_size
  - dim_M / dim_N / dim_K2 each divisible by their tile knobs
  - tile sizes >= pv intrinsic shape and <= 512 (VGPR cap, mirrors
    the matmul emitter)
  - tile-size factorization
    (m_tile == sg_m_cnt × sg_m_tcnt × pv_mma_m, …)
  - QK K1 dim divisible by qk_mma_k
  - sg_m_cnt in [1, 32], sg_n_cnt == 1, sg_num == 4 (Python tuner
    default)
  - QK/PV single-intrinsic_mn invariant
    (qk_mma_m == pv_mma_m, qk_mma_n == pv_mma_n) — mirrors the
    Python tuner's single `intrinsic_mn` SMT variable shared across
    both matmuls
  - 4 × 6 MMA-layout bindings via lookup ops + the
    qk_acc == pv_acc layout-match invariant (the Flash-Attention
    online-attention requirement that QK's output and PV's output
    live in the same per-subgroup layout)
  - use_col_major / can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input equivalences
    against the match_layout disjunctions on those bindings
  - per-matmul tile-based shared-memory budget with the
    `If(can_reuse, pv_shared / 2, pv_shared)` reuse term (matching
    Python's `pv_shared //= 2` approximation on reuse — exact for
    square tiles, slightly off otherwise)
  - is_valid_vector_distribute_mma_schedule (schedule_aligned +
    lhs/rhs distributable) for both QK and PV schedules

Decomposition-config also flows back to the tuner via a parallel
C++/C/Python helper triad:
  - materializeDecompositionConfigFromConstraints in
    MaterializeSMTConstraintAssignments (kDecompositionConfigKey
    promoted to SMTConstraintUtils.h so the emitter and materializer
    share one source of truth)
  - C API ireeCodegenMaterializeDecompositionConfigFromConstraintsOp
    (mirror of the existing ...CompilationInfoFromConstraintsOp)
  - Symbol exports in api_exports.{ld,def,macos.lst,c}
  - Python binding iree_codegen.materialize_decomposition_config

Other deferrals: only square-MN MMAs (m == n) are enumerated for the
attention path so the constraint body can use a single intrinsic_mn
variable; supporting non-square MMAs (e.g. VDMFMA_F32_8x16x64x2_F16)
is follow-up work that needs a paired (intrinsic_m, intrinsic_n)
variable. inferAttentionDimInfo asserts the v0 single-dim-per-role
restriction (m / n / k1 / k2 each contributing exactly one loop dim)
so multi-head shapes with multiple M dims fail loudly rather than
silently dropping outer dims.

Test coverage:
  - new config_llvm_gpu_vd_attention_constraints.mlir locks in the
    attention knob template (typed per-matmul LoweringConfigAttr
    with mma_kind/promote_operands/promotion_types/subgroup_basis,
    SMT-internal aux sub-dicts) plus CHECK-DAG for every constraint
    family (tile/factorization, sg counts, single-intrinsic_mn,
    layout bindings × 24, qk_acc == pv_acc invariant, use_col_major
    and can_reuse bools, schedule-validity for QK and PV).
  - verify_smt_constraints_e2e.mlir gets attention passing +
    violation splits in the new schema; passing case uses
    asymmetric m_tile / n_tile (128 / 64) so accidental axis swaps
    in the emitter would surface as verification failures rather
    than silently passing under symmetry.
  - tuner_api_test.py gets attention round-trips through both
    iree_codegen.materialize_compilation_info and the new
    iree_codegen.materialize_decomposition_config (happy path,
    indexed MMA selection, missing-assignment error).

Issue: https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/23535
Signed-off-by: Bangtian Liu <liubangtian@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[ROCM][Codegen] Add experimental amdgcn SPIR-V path (#24499)

Adds an experimental ROCm amdgcn SPIR-V path that emits HIP-loadable
SPIR-V instead of native HSACO, enabling the HIP runtime to JIT compile
device code for the target GPU. The main changes are:

- `--iree-rocm-use-spirv` flag to select `rocm-spirv-fb` for HIP
targets.
- ROCDL prepare for SPIR-V: Adjust address spaces, calling conventions,
remove AMDGPU-specific function attributes.
- ROCMTarget: Serialize LLVM SPIR-V output into a HIP-loadable offload
bundle.
- Focused lit coverage for lowering, serialization, command-line
handling.

---------

Signed-off-by: Austin Lu <aulu@amd.com>
Co-authored-by: Jakub Kuderski <jakub@nod-labs.com>
name: setup_metadata

commit_message:
[Codegen] Add VectorDistribute constraints for attention

Adds emitVectorDistributeAttentionConstraintsForOp +
buildVectorDistributeAttentionKnobsDict next to the existing
contraction/conv VectorDistribute versions in
LLVMGPUConstraintGenerator, and refactors emitVectorDistributeConstraintsForOp
to branch by op kind so OnlineAttentionOp routes through the new
emitter. emitMMALookup gains an `mmaIdxKnobName` parameter so the two
attention matmuls (QK and PV) carry distinct knobs without colliding
on "mma_idx", and returns the index knob alongside the shape lookups
so layout-binding can reuse it without redeclaring KnobOps.

Knob template (top-level) matches native attention codegen output
(KernelConfig.cpp's setAttention…):
  workgroup          ([1 at batch dims, m_tile on innermost M,
                       n_tile on innermost N])
  reduction          (red_k2 on innermost K2)
  promote_operands   ([0, 1, 2]) + promotion_types
                     ([derived_thread_config]*3)
  decomposition_config
    qk_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
    pv_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
  workgroup_size     ([wg_size_x, 1, 1])
  subgroup_size      (sg_size)

Per-matmul `lowering_config` entries are typed
`IREE::GPU::LoweringConfigAttr`s (not raw DictAttrs — attention
codegen casts them to LoweringConfigAttr, so a raw dict gets silently
rejected and codegen falls back to default per-matmul behavior).
Each carries mma_kind (one_of_knob<qk_mma_idx>/<pv_mma_idx>),
promote_operands + promotion_types (fixed [0,1]/[1] with
derived_thread_config), and subgroup_basis whose counts reference
the top-level sg_m_cnt / sg_n_cnt knobs at the M / N dim positions
(mapping projected per matmul: drop N for QK, drop K1 for PV).

In addition to the per-matmul lowering_config knobs above, the
template declares three SMT-only auxiliary sub-dictionaries that
codegen never reads (the materializer skips them; the verifier
whitelists them):
  smt_internal_subgroup_tile_counts — sg_m_tcnt / sg_n_tcnt / sg_k_tcnt
    factorize m_tile / n_tile / red_k2 into
    (subgroup_count × subgroup_tile_count × intrinsic_size) so the
    schedule-validity helper can reason about each factor.
  smt_internal_mma_layouts — 4 × 6 MMASingleSubgroupLayout fields
    (qk_acc / pv_lhs / pv_rhs / pv_acc each carrying element_x/y,
    thread_x/y, tstrides_x/y) bound to the chosen MMA via
    iree_codegen.smt.lookup ops over qk_mma_idx / pv_mma_idx.
  smt_internal_bools — use_col_major and
    can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input, encoded as int_knob ∈ {0, 1}
    (BoolKnobAttr doesn't exist yet); each constrained equivalent to
    a match_layout disjunction over the layout fields above.

Three pieces of generic infrastructure had to learn about typed
wrapper attrs to keep this end-to-end:

1. `hasKnobName` (ConstraintsOp::verify) rewritten with
   AttrTypeWalker so the verifier sees knob references nested inside
   any typed attribute, not just DictionaryAttr/ArrayAttr.

2. `materializeKnobAttribute` (MaterializeSMTConstraintAssignments)
   gains a LoweringConfigAttr case that recurses into the inner
   DictAttr and re-wraps the materialized result.

3. `extractKnobValue` (VerifyPipelineConstraints) gains a
   LoweringConfigAttr case + a generic Attribute-equality `Default`
   for fixed typed leaves like `#iree_gpu.derived_thread_config` in
   per-matmul promotion_types lists. `extractKnobValues` now
   distinguishes intentionally-absent SMT-only auxiliary keys (the
   three `smt_internal_*` sub-dicts) from real config drift: missing
   non-aux entries now fail verification instead of silently
   skipping every constraint that referenced them.

Constraint body ports `generate_attention_vector_distribute_constraints`
(sharktuner/dispatch_constraints.py:434-596) 1:1 — bijective parity
vs the legacy Python tuner is the gate (110 = 110 on the parity
fixture; see the parity-proof snapshots on the tuner side). The body
covers:
  - sg_size == preferred_subgroup_size
  - dim_M / dim_N / dim_K2 each divisible by their tile knobs
  - tile sizes >= pv intrinsic shape and <= 512 (VGPR cap, mirrors
    the matmul emitter)
  - tile-size factorization
    (m_tile == sg_m_cnt × sg_m_tcnt × pv_mma_m, …)
  - QK K1 dim divisible by qk_mma_k
  - sg_m_cnt in [1, 32], sg_n_cnt == 1, sg_num == 4 (Python tuner
    default)
  - QK/PV single-intrinsic_mn invariant
    (qk_mma_m == pv_mma_m, qk_mma_n == pv_mma_n) — mirrors the
    Python tuner's single `intrinsic_mn` SMT variable shared across
    both matmuls
  - 4 × 6 MMA-layout bindings via lookup ops + the
    qk_acc == pv_acc layout-match invariant (the Flash-Attention
    online-attention requirement that QK's output and PV's output
    live in the same per-subgroup layout)
  - use_col_major / can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input equivalences
    against the match_layout disjunctions on those bindings
  - per-matmul tile-based shared-memory budget with the
    `If(can_reuse, pv_shared / 2, pv_shared)` reuse term (matching
    Python's `pv_shared //= 2` approximation on reuse — exact for
    square tiles, slightly off otherwise)
  - is_valid_vector_distribute_mma_schedule (schedule_aligned +
    lhs/rhs distributable) for both QK and PV schedules

Decomposition-config also flows back to the tuner via a parallel
C++/C/Python helper triad:
  - materializeDecompositionConfigFromConstraints in
    MaterializeSMTConstraintAssignments (kDecompositionConfigKey
    promoted to SMTConstraintUtils.h so the emitter and materializer
    share one source of truth)
  - C API ireeCodegenMaterializeDecompositionConfigFromConstraintsOp
    (mirror of the existing ...CompilationInfoFromConstraintsOp)
  - Symbol exports in api_exports.{ld,def,macos.lst,c}
  - Python binding iree_codegen.materialize_decomposition_config

Other deferrals: only square-MN MMAs (m == n) are enumerated for the
attention path so the constraint body can use a single intrinsic_mn
variable; supporting non-square MMAs (e.g. VDMFMA_F32_8x16x64x2_F16)
is follow-up work that needs a paired (intrinsic_m, intrinsic_n)
variable. inferAttentionDimInfo asserts the v0 single-dim-per-role
restriction (m / n / k1 / k2 each contributing exactly one loop dim)
so multi-head shapes with multiple M dims fail loudly rather than
silently dropping outer dims.

Test coverage:
  - new config_llvm_gpu_vd_attention_constraints.mlir locks in the
    attention knob template (typed per-matmul LoweringConfigAttr
    with mma_kind/promote_operands/promotion_types/subgroup_basis,
    SMT-internal aux sub-dicts) plus CHECK-DAG for every constraint
    family (tile/factorization, sg counts, single-intrinsic_mn,
    layout bindings × 24, qk_acc == pv_acc invariant, use_col_major
    and can_reuse bools, schedule-validity for QK and PV).
  - verify_smt_constraints_e2e.mlir gets attention passing +
    violation splits in the new schema; passing case uses
    asymmetric m_tile / n_tile (128 / 64) so accidental axis swaps
    in the emitter would surface as verification failures rather
    than silently passing under symmetry.
  - tuner_api_test.py gets attention round-trips through both
    iree_codegen.materialize_compilation_info and the new
    iree_codegen.materialize_decomposition_config (happy path,
    indexed MMA selection, missing-assignment error).

Issue: https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/23535
Signed-off-by: Bangtian Liu <liubangtian@gmail.com>

on "mma_idx", and returns the index knob alongside the shape lookups
so layout-binding can reuse it without redeclaring KnobOps.

(KernelConfig.cpp's setAttention…):

                       n_tile on innermost N])
  reduction          (red_k2 on innermost K2)
  promote_operands   ([0, 1, 2]) + promotion_types
                     ([derived_thread_config]*3)
  decomposition_config
    qk_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
    pv_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
  workgroup_size     ([wg_size_x, 1, 1])
  subgroup_size      (sg_size)

Per-matmul `lowering_config` entries are typed
`IREE::GPU::LoweringConfigAttr`s (not raw DictAttrs — attention
codegen casts them to LoweringConfigAttr, so a raw dict gets silently
rejected and codegen falls back to default per-matmul behavior).
Each carries mma_kind (one_of_knob<qk_mma_idx>/<pv_mma_idx>),
promote_operands + promotion_types (fixed [0,1]/[1] with
derived_thread_config), and subgroup_basis whose counts reference
the top-level sg_m_cnt / sg_n_cnt knobs at the M / N dim positions
(mapping projected per matmul: drop N for QK, drop K1 for PV).

codegen never reads (the materializer skips them; the verifier
whitelists them):

    factorize m_tile / n_tile / red_k2 into
    (subgroup_count × subgroup_tile_count × intrinsic_size) so the
    schedule-validity helper can reason about each factor.

  decomposition_config

    pv_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>

  subgroup_size      (sg_size)

whitelists them):

    schedule-validity helper can reason about each factor.

Adds emitVectorDistributeAttentionConstraintsForOp +
buildVectorDistributeAttentionKnobsDict next to the existing
contraction/conv VectorDistribute versions in
LLVMGPUConstraintGenerator, and refactors emitVectorDistributeConstraintsForOp
to branch by op kind so OnlineAttentionOp routes through the new
emitter. emitMMALookup gains an `mmaIdxKnobName` parameter so the two
attention matmuls (QK and PV) carry distinct knobs without colliding
on "mma_idx", and returns the index knob alongside the shape lookups
so layout-binding can reuse it without redeclaring KnobOps.

Knob template (top-level) matches native attention codegen output
(KernelConfig.cpp's setAttention…):
  workgroup          ([1 at batch dims, m_tile on innermost M,
                       n_tile on innermost N])
  reduction          (red_k2 on innermost K2)
  promote_operands   ([0, 1, 2]) + promotion_types
                     ([derived_thread_config]*3)
  decomposition_config
    qk_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
    pv_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
  workgroup_size     ([wg_size_x, 1, 1])
  subgroup_size      (sg_size)

Per-matmul `lowering_config` entries are typed
`IREE::GPU::LoweringConfigAttr`s (not raw DictAttrs — attention
codegen casts them to LoweringConfigAttr, so a raw dict gets silently
rejected and codegen falls back to default per-matmul behavior).
Each carries mma_kind (one_of_knob<qk_mma_idx>/<pv_mma_idx>),
promote_operands + promotion_types (fixed [0,1]/[1] with
derived_thread_config), and subgroup_basis whose counts reference
the top-level sg_m_cnt / sg_n_cnt knobs at the M / N dim positions
(mapping projected per matmul: drop N for QK, drop K1 for PV).

In addition to the per-matmul lowering_config knobs above, the
template declares three SMT-only auxiliary sub-dictionaries that
codegen never reads (the materializer skips them; the verifier
whitelists them):
  smt_internal_subgroup_tile_counts — sg_m_tcnt / sg_n_tcnt / sg_k_tcnt
    factorize m_tile / n_tile / red_k2 into
    (subgroup_count × subgroup_tile_count × intrinsic_size) so the
    schedule-validity helper can reason about each factor.
  smt_internal_mma_layouts — 4 × 6 MMASingleSubgroupLayout fields
    (qk_acc / pv_lhs / pv_rhs / pv_acc each carrying element_x/y,
    thread_x/y, tstrides_x/y) bound to the chosen MMA via
    iree_codegen.smt.lookup ops over qk_mma_idx / pv_mma_idx.
  smt_internal_bools — use_col_major and
    can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input, encoded as int_knob ∈ {0, 1}
    (BoolKnobAttr doesn't exist yet); each constrained equivalent to
    a match_layout disjunction over the layout fields above.

Three pieces of generic infrastructure had to learn about typed
wrapper attrs to keep this end-to-end:

1. `hasKnobName` (ConstraintsOp::verify) rewritten with
   AttrTypeWalker so the verifier sees knob references nested inside
   any typed attribute, not just DictionaryAttr/ArrayAttr.

2. `materializeKnobAttribute` (MaterializeSMTConstraintAssignments)
   gains a LoweringConfigAttr case that recurses into the inner
   DictAttr and re-wraps the materialized result.

   LoweringConfigAttr case + a generic Attribute-equality `Default`
   for fixed typed leaves like `#iree_gpu.derived_thread_config` in
   per-matmul promotion_types lists. `extractKnobValues` now
   distinguishes intentionally-absent SMT-only auxiliary keys (the
   three `smt_internal_*` sub-dicts) from real config drift: missing
   non-aux entries now fail verification instead of silently
   skipping every constraint that referenced them.

Constraint body ports `generate_attention_vector_distribute_constraints`
(sharktuner/dispatch_constraints.py:434-596) 1:1 — bijective parity
vs the legacy Python tuner is the gate (110 = 110 on the parity
fixture; see the parity-proof snapshots on the tuner side). The body
covers:
  - sg_size == preferred_subgroup_size
  - dim_M / dim_N / dim_K2 each divisible by their tile knobs
  - tile sizes >= pv intrinsic shape and <= 512 (VGPR cap, mirrors
    the matmul emitter)
  - tile-size factorization
    (m_tile == sg_m_cnt × sg_m_tcnt × pv_mma_m, …)
  - QK K1 dim divisible by qk_mma_k
  - sg_m_cnt in [1, 32], sg_n_cnt == 1, sg_num == 4 (Python tuner
    default)
  - QK/PV single-intrinsic_mn invariant
    (qk_mma_m == pv_mma_m, qk_mma_n == pv_mma_n) — mirrors the
    Python tuner's single `intrinsic_mn` SMT variable shared across
    both matmuls
  - 4 × 6 MMA-layout bindings via lookup ops + the
    qk_acc == pv_acc layout-match invariant (the Flash-Attention
    online-attention requirement that QK's output and PV's output
    live in the same per-subgroup layout)
  - use_col_major / can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input equivalences
    against the match_layout disjunctions on those bindings
  - per-matmul tile-based shared-memory budget with the
    `If(can_reuse, pv_shared / 2, pv_shared)` reuse term (matching
    Python's `pv_shared //= 2` approximation on reuse — exact for
    square tiles, slightly off otherwise)

buildVectorDistributeAttentionKnobsDict next to the existing
contraction/conv VectorDistribute versions in

to branch by op kind so OnlineAttentionOp routes through the new
emitter. emitMMALookup gains an `mmaIdxKnobName` parameter so the two
attention matmuls (QK and PV) carry distinct knobs without colliding
on "mma_idx", and returns the index knob alongside the shape lookups
so layout-binding can reuse it without redeclaring KnobOps.

Knob template (top-level) matches native attention codegen output
(KernelConfig.cpp's setAttention…):
  workgroup          ([1 at batch dims, m_tile on innermost M,
                       n_tile on innermost N])
  reduction          (red_k2 on innermost K2)
  promote_operands   ([0, 1, 2]) + promotion_types
                     ([derived_thread_config]*3)
  decomposition_config
    qk_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
    pv_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
  workgroup_size     ([wg_size_x, 1, 1])
  subgroup_size      (sg_size)

Per-matmul `lowering_config` entries are typed
`IREE::GPU::LoweringConfigAttr`s (not raw DictAttrs — attention
codegen casts them to LoweringConfigAttr, so a raw dict gets silently
rejected and codegen falls back to default per-matmul behavior).
Each carries mma_kind (one_of_knob<qk_mma_idx>/<pv_mma_idx>),
promote_operands + promotion_types (fixed [0,1]/[1] with
derived_thread_config), and subgroup_basis whose counts reference
the top-level sg_m_cnt / sg_n_cnt knobs at the M / N dim positions
(mapping projected per matmul: drop N for QK, drop K1 for PV).

template declares three SMT-only auxiliary sub-dictionaries that
codegen never reads (the materializer skips them; the verifier
whitelists them):
  smt_internal_subgroup_tile_counts — sg_m_tcnt / sg_n_tcnt / sg_k_tcnt
    factorize m_tile / n_tile / red_k2 into
    (subgroup_count × subgroup_tile_count × intrinsic_size) so the
    schedule-validity helper can reason about each factor.

    thread_x/y, tstrides_x/y) bound to the chosen MMA via
    iree_codegen.smt.lookup ops over qk_mma_idx / pv_mma_idx.
  smt_internal_bools — use_col_major and
    can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input, encoded as int_knob ∈ {0, 1}
    (BoolKnobAttr doesn't exist yet); each constrained equivalent to
    a match_layout disjunction over the layout fields above.

Adds emitVectorDistributeAttentionConstraintsForOp +
buildVectorDistributeAttentionKnobsDict next to the existing
contraction/conv VectorDistribute versions in
LLVMGPUConstraintGenerator, and refactors emitVectorDistributeConstraintsForOp
to branch by op kind so OnlineAttentionOp routes through the new
emitter. emitMMALookup gains an `mmaIdxKnobName` parameter so the two
attention matmuls (QK and PV) carry distinct knobs without colliding
on "mma_idx", and returns the index knob alongside the shape lookups
so layout-binding can reuse it without redeclaring KnobOps.

Knob template (top-level) matches native attention codegen output
(KernelConfig.cpp's setAttention…):
  workgroup          ([1 at batch dims, m_tile on innermost M,
                       n_tile on innermost N])
  reduction          (red_k2 on innermost K2)
  promote_operands   ([0, 1, 2]) + promotion_types
                     ([derived_thread_config]*3)
  decomposition_config
    qk_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
    pv_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
  workgroup_size     ([wg_size_x, 1, 1])
  subgroup_size      (sg_size)

Per-matmul `lowering_config` entries are typed
`IREE::GPU::LoweringConfigAttr`s (not raw DictAttrs — attention
codegen casts them to LoweringConfigAttr, so a raw dict gets silently
rejected and codegen falls back to default per-matmul behavior).
Each carries mma_kind (one_of_knob<qk_mma_idx>/<pv_mma_idx>),
promote_operands + promotion_types (fixed [0,1]/[1] with
derived_thread_config), and subgroup_basis whose counts reference
the top-level sg_m_cnt / sg_n_cnt knobs at the M / N dim positions
(mapping projected per matmul: drop N for QK, drop K1 for PV).

In addition to the per-matmul lowering_config knobs above, the
template declares three SMT-only auxiliary sub-dictionaries that
codegen never reads (the materializer skips them; the verifier
whitelists them):
  smt_internal_subgroup_tile_counts — sg_m_tcnt / sg_n_tcnt / sg_k_tcnt
    factorize m_tile / n_tile / red_k2 into
    (subgroup_count × subgroup_tile_count × intrinsic_size) so the
    schedule-validity helper can reason about each factor.
  smt_internal_mma_layouts — 4 × 6 MMASingleSubgroupLayout fields
    (qk_acc / pv_lhs / pv_rhs / pv_acc each carrying element_x/y,
    thread_x/y, tstrides_x/y) bound to the chosen MMA via
    iree_codegen.smt.lookup ops over qk_mma_idx / pv_mma_idx.
  smt_internal_bools — use_col_major and
    can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input, encoded as int_knob ∈ {0, 1}
    (BoolKnobAttr doesn't exist yet); each constrained equivalent to
    a match_layout disjunction over the layout fields above.

Three pieces of generic infrastructure had to learn about typed
wrapper attrs to keep this end-to-end:

1. `hasKnobName` (ConstraintsOp::verify) rewritten with
   AttrTypeWalker so the verifier sees knob references nested inside
   any typed attribute, not just DictionaryAttr/ArrayAttr.

2. `materializeKnobAttribute` (MaterializeSMTConstraintAssignments)
   gains a LoweringConfigAttr case that recurses into the inner
   DictAttr and re-wraps the materialized result.

3. `extractKnobValue` (VerifyPipelineConstraints) gains a
   LoweringConfigAttr case + a generic Attribute-equality `Default`
   for fixed typed leaves like `#iree_gpu.derived_thread_config` in
   per-matmul promotion_types lists. `extractKnobValues` now
   distinguishes intentionally-absent SMT-only auxiliary keys (the
   three `smt_internal_*` sub-dicts) from real config drift: missing
   non-aux entries now fail verification instead of silently
   skipping every constraint that referenced them.

Constraint body ports `generate_attention_vector_distribute_constraints`
(sharktuner/dispatch_constraints.py:434-596) 1:1 — bijective parity
vs the legacy Python tuner is the gate (110 = 110 on the parity
fixture; see the parity-proof snapshots on the tuner side). The body
covers:
  - sg_size == preferred_subgroup_size
  - dim_M / dim_N / dim_K2 each divisible by their tile knobs
  - tile sizes >= pv intrinsic shape and <= 512 (VGPR cap, mirrors
    the matmul emitter)
  - tile-size factorization
    (m_tile == sg_m_cnt × sg_m_tcnt × pv_mma_m, …)
  - QK K1 dim divisible by qk_mma_k
  - sg_m_cnt in [1, 32], sg_n_cnt == 1, sg_num == 4 (Python tuner
    default)
  - QK/PV single-intrinsic_mn invariant
    (qk_mma_m == pv_mma_m, qk_mma_n == pv_mma_n) — mirrors the
    Python tuner's single `intrinsic_mn` SMT variable shared across
    both matmuls
  - 4 × 6 MMA-layout bindings via lookup ops + the
    qk_acc == pv_acc layout-match invariant (the Flash-Attention
    online-attention requirement that QK's output and PV's output
    live in the same per-subgroup layout)
  - use_col_major / can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input equivalences
    against the match_layout disjunctions on those bindings
  - per-matmul tile-based shared-memory budget with the
    `If(can_reuse, pv_shared / 2, pv_shared)` reuse term (matching
    Python's `pv_shared //= 2` approximation on reuse — exact for
    square tiles, slightly off otherwise)

Adds emitVectorDistributeAttentionConstraintsForOp +
buildVectorDistributeAttentionKnobsDict next to the existing
contraction/conv VectorDistribute versions in
LLVMGPUConstraintGenerator, and refactors emitVectorDistributeConstraintsForOp
to branch by op kind so OnlineAttentionOp routes through the new
emitter. emitMMALookup gains an `mmaIdxKnobName` parameter so the two
attention matmuls (QK and PV) carry distinct knobs without colliding
on "mma_idx", and returns the index knob alongside the shape lookups
so layout-binding can reuse it without redeclaring KnobOps.

Knob template (top-level) matches native attention codegen output
(KernelConfig.cpp's setAttention…):
  workgroup          ([1 at batch dims, m_tile on innermost M,
                       n_tile on innermost N])
  reduction          (red_k2 on innermost K2)
  promote_operands   ([0, 1, 2]) + promotion_types
                     ([derived_thread_config]*3)
  decomposition_config
    qk_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
    pv_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
  workgroup_size     ([wg_size_x, 1, 1])
  subgroup_size      (sg_size)

Per-matmul `lowering_config` entries are typed
`IREE::GPU::LoweringConfigAttr`s (not raw DictAttrs — attention
codegen casts them to LoweringConfigAttr, so a raw dict gets silently
rejected and codegen falls back to default per-matmul behavior).
Each carries mma_kind (one_of_knob<qk_mma_idx>/<pv_mma_idx>),
promote_operands + promotion_types (fixed [0,1]/[1] with
derived_thread_config), and subgroup_basis whose counts reference
the top-level sg_m_cnt / sg_n_cnt knobs at the M / N dim positions
(mapping projected per matmul: drop N for QK, drop K1 for PV).

In addition to the per-matmul lowering_config knobs above, the
template declares three SMT-only auxiliary sub-dictionaries that
codegen never reads (the materializer skips them; the verifier
whitelists them):
  smt_internal_subgroup_tile_counts — sg_m_tcnt / sg_n_tcnt / sg_k_tcnt
    factorize m_tile / n_tile / red_k2 into
    (subgroup_count × subgroup_tile_count × intrinsic_size) so the
    schedule-validity helper can reason about each factor.
  smt_internal_mma_layouts — 4 × 6 MMASingleSubgroupLayout fields
    (qk_acc / pv_lhs / pv_rhs / pv_acc each carrying element_x/y,
    thread_x/y, tstrides_x/y) bound to the chosen MMA via
    iree_codegen.smt.lookup ops over qk_mma_idx / pv_mma_idx.
  smt_internal_bools — use_col_major and
    can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input, encoded as int_knob ∈ {0, 1}
    (BoolKnobAttr doesn't exist yet); each constrained equivalent to
    a match_layout disjunction over the layout fields above.

wrapper attrs to keep this end-to-end:

1. `hasKnobName` (ConstraintsOp::verify) rewritten with
   AttrTypeWalker so the verifier sees knob references nested inside
   any typed attribute, not just DictionaryAttr/ArrayAttr.

   non-aux entries now fail verification instead of silently
   skipping every constraint that referenced them.

buildVectorDistributeAttentionKnobsDict next to the existing
contraction/conv VectorDistribute versions in
LLVMGPUConstraintGenerator, and refactors emitVectorDistributeConstraintsForOp
to branch by op kind so OnlineAttentionOp routes through the new
emitter. emitMMALookup gains an `mmaIdxKnobName` parameter so the two
attention matmuls (QK and PV) carry distinct knobs without colliding
on "mma_idx", and returns the index knob alongside the shape lookups
so layout-binding can reuse it without redeclaring KnobOps.

Knob template (top-level) matches native attention codegen output
(KernelConfig.cpp's setAttention…):
  workgroup          ([1 at batch dims, m_tile on innermost M,
                       n_tile on innermost N])
  reduction          (red_k2 on innermost K2)
  promote_operands   ([0, 1, 2]) + promotion_types
                     ([derived_thread_config]*3)
  decomposition_config
    qk_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
    pv_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
  workgroup_size     ([wg_size_x, 1, 1])
  subgroup_size      (sg_size)

Per-matmul `lowering_config` entries are typed
`IREE::GPU::LoweringConfigAttr`s (not raw DictAttrs — attention
codegen casts them to LoweringConfigAttr, so a raw dict gets silently
rejected and codegen falls back to default per-matmul behavior).
Each carries mma_kind (one_of_knob<qk_mma_idx>/<pv_mma_idx>),
promote_operands + promotion_types (fixed [0,1]/[1] with
derived_thread_config), and subgroup_basis whose counts reference
the top-level sg_m_cnt / sg_n_cnt knobs at the M / N dim positions
(mapping projected per matmul: drop N for QK, drop K1 for PV).

In addition to the per-matmul lowering_config knobs above, the
template declares three SMT-only auxiliary sub-dictionaries that
codegen never reads (the materializer skips them; the verifier
whitelists them):
  smt_internal_subgroup_tile_counts — sg_m_tcnt / sg_n_tcnt / sg_k_tcnt
    factorize m_tile / n_tile / red_k2 into
    (subgroup_count × subgroup_tile_count × intrinsic_size) so the
    schedule-validity helper can reason about each factor.
  smt_internal_mma_layouts — 4 × 6 MMASingleSubgroupLayout fields
    (qk_acc / pv_lhs / pv_rhs / pv_acc each carrying element_x/y,
    thread_x/y, tstrides_x/y) bound to the chosen MMA via
    iree_codegen.smt.lookup ops over qk_mma_idx / pv_mma_idx.
  smt_internal_bools — use_col_major and
    can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input, encoded as int_knob ∈ {0, 1}
    (BoolKnobAttr doesn't exist yet); each constrained equivalent to
    a match_layout disjunction over the layout fields above.

wrapper attrs to keep this end-to-end:

1. `hasKnobName` (ConstraintsOp::verify) rewritten with
   AttrTypeWalker so the verifier sees knob references nested inside
   any typed attribute, not just DictionaryAttr/ArrayAttr.

   gains a LoweringConfigAttr case that recurses into the inner
   DictAttr and re-wraps the materialized result.

   LoweringConfigAttr case + a generic Attribute-equality `Default`

   distinguishes intentionally-absent SMT-only auxiliary keys (the
   three `smt_internal_*` sub-dicts) from real config drift: missing
   non-aux entries now fail verification instead of silently
   skipping every constraint that referenced them.

(sharktuner/dispatch_constraints.py:434-596) 1:1 — bijective parity
vs the legacy Python tuner is the gate (110 = 110 on the parity
fixture; see the parity-proof snapshots on the tuner side). The body
covers:

  - dim_M / dim_N / dim_K2 each divisible by their tile knobs
  - tile sizes >= pv intrinsic shape and <= 512 (VGPR cap, mirrors
    the matmul emitter)
  - tile-size factorization
    (m_tile == sg_m_cnt × sg_m_tcnt × pv_mma_m, …)
  - QK K1 dim divisible by qk_mma_k
  - sg_m_cnt in [1, 32], sg_n_cnt == 1, sg_num == 4 (Python tuner
    default)
  - QK/PV single-intrinsic_mn invariant
    (qk_mma_m == pv_mma_m, qk_mma_n == pv_mma_n) — mirrors the

    both matmuls

    online-attention requirement that QK's output and PV's output
    live in the same per-subgroup layout)
  - use_col_major / can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input equivalences
    against the match_layout disjunctions on those bindings

  promote_operands   ([0, 1, 2]) + promotion_types
                     ([derived_thread_config]*3)

    pv_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>

  subgroup_size      (sg_size)

rejected and codegen falls back to default per-matmul behavior).

the top-level sg_m_cnt / sg_n_cnt knobs at the M / N dim positions

whitelists them):

to branch by op kind so OnlineAttentionOp routes through the new
emitter. emitMMALookup gains an `mmaIdxKnobName` parameter so the two
attention matmuls (QK and PV) carry distinct knobs without colliding
on "mma_idx", and returns the index knob alongside the shape lookups
so layout-binding can reuse it without redeclaring KnobOps.

Knob template (top-level) matches native attention codegen output
(KernelConfig.cpp's setAttention…):
  workgroup          ([1 at batch dims, m_tile on innermost M,
                       n_tile on innermost N])
  reduction          (red_k2 on innermost K2)
  promote_operands   ([0, 1, 2]) + promotion_types
                     ([derived_thread_config]*3)
  decomposition_config
    qk_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
    pv_attrs.lowering_config = #iree_gpu.lowering_config<{...}>
  workgroup_size     ([wg_size_x, 1, 1])
  subgroup_size      (sg_size)

Per-matmul `lowering_config` entries are typed
`IREE::GPU::LoweringConfigAttr`s (not raw DictAttrs — attention
codegen casts them to LoweringConfigAttr, so a raw dict gets silently
rejected and codegen falls back to default per-matmul behavior).
Each carries mma_kind (one_of_knob<qk_mma_idx>/<pv_mma_idx>),
promote_operands + promotion_types (fixed [0,1]/[1] with
derived_thread_config), and subgroup_basis whose counts reference
the top-level sg_m_cnt / sg_n_cnt knobs at the M / N dim positions
(mapping projected per matmul: drop N for QK, drop K1 for PV).

In addition to the per-matmul lowering_config knobs above, the
template declares three SMT-only auxiliary sub-dictionaries that
codegen never reads (the materializer skips them; the verifier
whitelists them):
  smt_internal_subgroup_tile_counts — sg_m_tcnt / sg_n_tcnt / sg_k_tcnt
    factorize m_tile / n_tile / red_k2 into
    (subgroup_count × subgroup_tile_count × intrinsic_size) so the
    schedule-validity helper can reason about each factor.
  smt_internal_mma_layouts — 4 × 6 MMASingleSubgroupLayout fields
    (qk_acc / pv_lhs / pv_rhs / pv_acc each carrying element_x/y,
    thread_x/y, tstrides_x/y) bound to the chosen MMA via
    iree_codegen.smt.lookup ops over qk_mma_idx / pv_mma_idx.
  smt_internal_bools — use_col_major and
    can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input, encoded as int_knob ∈ {0, 1}
    (BoolKnobAttr doesn't exist yet); each constrained equivalent to
    a match_layout disjunction over the layout fields above.

Three pieces of generic infrastructure had to learn about typed
wrapper attrs to keep this end-to-end:

1. `hasKnobName` (ConstraintsOp::verify) rewritten with
   AttrTypeWalker so the verifier sees knob references nested inside
   any typed attribute, not just DictionaryAttr/ArrayAttr.

2. `materializeKnobAttribute` (MaterializeSMTConstraintAssignments)
   gains a LoweringConfigAttr case that recurses into the inner
   DictAttr and re-wraps the materialized result.

3. `extractKnobValue` (VerifyPipelineConstraints) gains a
   LoweringConfigAttr case + a generic Attribute-equality `Default`
   for fixed typed leaves like `#iree_gpu.derived_thread_config` in
   per-matmul promotion_types lists. `extractKnobValues` now
   distinguishes intentionally-absent SMT-only auxiliary keys (the
   three `smt_internal_*` sub-dicts) from real config drift: missing
   non-aux entries now fail verification instead of silently
   skipping every constraint that referenced them.

Constraint body ports `generate_attention_vector_distribute_constraints`
(sharktuner/dispatch_constraints.py:434-596) 1:1 — bijective parity
vs the legacy Python tuner is the gate (110 = 110 on the parity
fixture; see the parity-proof snapshots on the tuner side). The body
covers:
  - sg_size == preferred_subgroup_size
  - dim_M / dim_N / dim_K2 each divisible by their tile knobs
  - tile sizes >= pv intrinsic shape and <= 512 (VGPR cap, mirrors
    the matmul emitter)
  - tile-size factorization
    (m_tile == sg_m_cnt × sg_m_tcnt × pv_mma_m, …)
  - QK K1 dim divisible by qk_mma_k
  - sg_m_cnt in [1, 32], sg_n_cnt == 1, sg_num == 4 (Python tuner
    default)
  - QK/PV single-intrinsic_mn invariant
    (qk_mma_m == pv_mma_m, qk_mma_n == pv_mma_n) — mirrors the
    Python tuner's single `intrinsic_mn` SMT variable shared across
    both matmuls
  - 4 × 6 MMA-layout bindings via lookup ops + the
    qk_acc == pv_acc layout-match invariant (the Flash-Attention
    online-attention requirement that QK's output and PV's output
    live in the same per-subgroup layout)
  - use_col_major / can_reuse_qk_output_for_pv_input equivalences
    against the match_layout disjunctions on those bindings
  - per-matmul tile-based shared-memory budget with the
    `If(can_reuse, pv_shared / 2, pv_shared)` reuse term (matching
    Python's `pv_shared //= 2` approximation on reuse — exact for
    square tiles, slightly off otherwise)
  - is_valid_vector_distribute_mma_schedule (schedule_aligned +
    lhs/rhs distributable) for both QK and PV schedules

Decomposition-config also flows back to the tuner via a parallel
C++/C/Python helper triad:
  - materializeDecompositionConfigFromConstraints in
    MaterializeSMTConstraintAssignments (kDecompositionConfigKey
    promoted to SMTConstraintUtils.h so the emitter and materializer
    share one source of truth)
  - C API ireeCodegenMaterializeDecompositionConfigFromConstraintsOp
    (mirror of the existing ...CompilationInfoFromConstraintsOp)
  - Symbol exports in api_exports.{ld,def,macos.lst,c}
  - Python binding iree_codegen.materialize_decomposition_config

Other deferrals: only square-MN MMAs (m == n) are enumerated for the
attention path so the constraint body can use a single intrinsic_mn
variable; supporting non-square MMAs (e.g. VDMFMA_F32_8x16x64x2_F16)
is follow-up work that needs a paired (intrinsic_m, intrinsic_n)
variable. inferAttentionDimInfo asserts the v0 single-dim-per-role
restriction (m / n / k1 / k2 each contributing exactly one loop dim)
so multi-head shapes with multiple M dims fail loudly rather than
silently dropping outer dims.

Test coverage:
  - new config_llvm_gpu_vd_attention_constraints.mlir locks in the
    attention knob template (typed per-matmul LoweringConfigAttr
    with mma_kind/promote_operands/promotion_types/subgroup_basis,
    SMT-internal aux sub-dicts) plus CHECK-DAG for every constraint
    family (tile/factorization, sg counts, single-intrinsic_mn,
    layout bindings × 24, qk_acc == pv_acc invariant, use_col_major
    and can_reuse bools, schedule-validity for QK and PV).
  - verify_smt_constraints_e2e.mlir gets attention passing +
    violation splits in the new schema; passing case uses
    asymmetric m_tile / n_tile (128 / 64) so accidental axis swaps
    in the emitter would surface as verification failures rather
    than silently passing under symmetry.
  - tuner_api_test.py gets attention round-trips through both
    iree_codegen.materialize_compilation_info and the new
    iree_codegen.materialize_decomposition_config (happy path,
    indexed MMA selection, missing-assignment error).

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Flatten contiguous trailing dims of transfers before unrolling.

`VectorTransferLoweringPass` applies the MLIR transfer-lowering patterns
with `maxTransferRank=1` plus full-unroll, which fully unrolls any
rank-N>1 `vector.transfer_read`/`transfer_write` to multiple rank-1
transfers (one per index of the outer dim). For multi-dim tiles whose
trailing dim is a tiny contiguous chunk, this unrolls a single wide
load into many narrow ones, which then have to be reassembled into a
wide vector via a chain of `shufflevector`s in the hot inner loop.

Example surfacing the cost: a 4096x4096 dynamic-shape bf16xbf16->f32
matmul with `--iree-llvmcpu-enable-inner-tiled` on Zen 4 lowered to
inner_tiled with N=16, K_inner=2. The RHS for one K-step is a
`vector<16x2xbf16>` from a contiguous 64-byte slice. Unrolling to 16
separate `<2 x bfloat>` loads forced a sequence of `vpermt2d`/
`vpermt2q` per K-iteration in the inner loop to rebuild the wide
RHS register — accounting for ~3 cycles of extra work per K-step on
top of the 29 dpbf16ps doing the real work.

Apply `populateFlattenVectorTransferPatterns` *before* the
rank-reduction patterns. It rewrites a multi-dim transfer with
contiguous trailing dims into a transfer on a `memref.collapse_shape`
view + a `vector.shape_cast`, so the read ends up as a single 1-D
transfer over the collapsed view and lowers to one wide `vector.load`.
Per-fragment effect on the matmul benchmark above: 80.8 ms -> 67.1 ms
(1.20x). Combined with the m_bcst-fold broadcast routing in a sibling
commit, end-to-end gets to 53.4 ms (within 5% of the precompiled
mmt4d ukernel at 50.9 ms).

Gate the flattening on the trailing-dim bitwidth, passing
`targetVectorBitwidth = 64`: only flatten transfers whose innermost dim
is a sub-64-bit chunk. A transfer whose innermost dim is already a
register-fraction-sized chunk (`<4xf32>`, `<8xf32>`, `<16xf32>`, ...)
tiles fine via plain rank reduction; flattening *that* would fuse the
rows into one oversized 1-D transfer and then re-split it with a
`vector.shape_cast` (a chain of extracts), inflating generated code
size with no benefit and regressing whole-model .vmfb size. The packed
inner-tile K dimensions that motivate this change are all <= 32 bits,
so they are still flattened.

Test fallout: `transpose_mask` in vector_lowering now writes a constant
`vector<4x2xi1>` mask (trailing dim 2 bits) as a single flat
`vector<8xi1>` store rather than per-row; strictly fewer ops, updated
the CHECK lines to match.

Progress towards #24515.

Signed-off-by: Benoit Jacob <jacob.benoit.1@gmail.com>

with `maxTransferRank=1` plus full-unroll, which fully unrolls any
rank-N>1 `vector.transfer_read`/`transfer_write` to multiple rank-1
transfers (one per index of the outer dim). For multi-dim tiles whose
trailing dim is a tiny contiguous chunk, this unrolls a single wide
load into many narrow ones, which then have to be reassembled into a
wide vector via a chain of `shufflevector`s in the hot inner loop.

Example surfacing the cost: a 4096x4096 dynamic-shape bf16xbf16->f32
matmul with `--iree-llvmcpu-enable-inner-tiled` on Zen 4 lowered to
inner_tiled with N=16, K_inner=2. The RHS for one K-step is a
`vector<16x2xbf16>` from a contiguous 64-byte slice. Unrolling to 16
separate `<2 x bfloat>` loads forced a sequence of `vpermt2d`/
`vpermt2q` per K-iteration in the inner loop to rebuild the wide
RHS register — accounting for ~3 cycles of extra work per K-step on
top of the 29 dpbf16ps doing the real work.

Apply `populateFlattenVectorTransferPatterns` *before* the
rank-reduction patterns. It rewrites a multi-dim transfer with
contiguous trailing dims into a transfer on a `memref.collapse_shape`
view + a `vector.shape_cast`, so the read ends up as a single 1-D
transfer over the collapsed view and lowers to one wide `vector.load`.
Per-fragment effect on the matmul benchmark above: 80.8 ms -> 67.1 ms
(1.20x). Combined with the m_bcst-fold broadcast routing in a sibling
commit, end-to-end gets to 53.4 ms (within 5% of the precompiled
mmt4d ukernel at 50.9 ms).

Gate the flattening on the trailing-dim bitwidth, passing
`targetVectorBitwidth = 64`: only flatten transfers whose innermost dim
is a sub-64-bit chunk. A transfer whose innermost dim is already a
register-fraction-sized chunk (`<4xf32>`, `<8xf32>`, `<16xf32>`, ...)
tiles fine via plain rank reduction; flattening *that* would fuse the
rows into one oversized 1-D transfer and then re-split it with a
`vector.shape_cast` (a chain of extracts), inflating generated code
size with no benefit and regressing whole-model .vmfb size. The packed
inner-tile K dimensions that motivate this change are all <= 32 bits,
so they are still flattened.

trailing dim is a tiny contiguous chunk, this unrolls a single wide
load into many narrow ones, which then have to be reassembled into a
wide vector via a chain of `shufflevector`s in the hot inner loop.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Flatten contiguous trailing dims of transfers before unrolling.

`VectorTransferLoweringPass` applies the MLIR transfer-lowering patterns
with `maxTransferRank=1` plus full-unroll, which fully unrolls any
rank-N>1 `vector.transfer_read`/`transfer_write` to multiple rank-1
transfers (one per index of the outer dim). For multi-dim tiles whose
trailing dim is a tiny contiguous chunk, this unrolls a single wide
load into many narrow ones, which then have to be reassembled into a
wide vector via a chain of `shufflevector`s in the hot inner loop.

Example surfacing the cost: a 4096x4096 dynamic-shape bf16xbf16->f32
matmul with `--iree-llvmcpu-enable-inner-tiled` on Zen 4 lowered to
inner_tiled with N=16, K_inner=2. The RHS for one K-step is a
`vector<16x2xbf16>` from a contiguous 64-byte slice. Unrolling to 16
separate `<2 x bfloat>` loads forced a sequence of `vpermt2d`/
`vpermt2q` per K-iteration in the inner loop to rebuild the wide
RHS register — accounting for ~3 cycles of extra work per K-step on
top of the 29 dpbf16ps doing the real work.

Apply `populateFlattenVectorTransferPatterns` *before* the
rank-reduction patterns. It rewrites a multi-dim transfer with
contiguous trailing dims into a transfer on a `memref.collapse_shape`
view + a `vector.shape_cast`, so the read ends up as a single 1-D
transfer over the collapsed view and lowers to one wide `vector.load`.
Per-fragment effect on the matmul benchmark above: 80.8 ms -> 67.1 ms
(1.20x). Combined with the m_bcst-fold broadcast routing in a sibling
commit, end-to-end gets to 53.4 ms (within 5% of the precompiled
mmt4d ukernel at 50.9 ms).

Gate the flattening on the trailing-dim bitwidth, passing
`targetVectorBitwidth = 64`: only flatten transfers whose innermost dim
is a sub-64-bit chunk. A transfer whose innermost dim is already a
register-fraction-sized chunk (`<4xf32>`, `<8xf32>`, `<16xf32>`, ...)
tiles fine via plain rank reduction; flattening *that* would fuse the
rows into one oversized 1-D transfer and then re-split it with a
`vector.shape_cast` (a chain of extracts), inflating generated code
size with no benefit and regressing whole-model .vmfb size. The packed
inner-tile K dimensions that motivate this change are all <= 32 bits,
so they are still flattened.

Test fallout: `transpose_mask` in vector_lowering now writes a constant
`vector<4x2xi1>` mask (trailing dim 2 bits) as a single flat
`vector<8xi1>` store rather than per-row; strictly fewer ops, updated

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Flatten contiguous trailing dims of transfers before unrolling.

`VectorTransferLoweringPass` applies the MLIR transfer-lowering patterns
with `maxTransferRank=1` plus full-unroll, which fully unrolls any
rank-N>1 `vector.transfer_read`/`transfer_write` to multiple rank-1
transfers (one per index of the outer dim). For multi-dim tiles whose
trailing dims are contiguous in memory, this unrolls a single wide
load into many narrow ones, which then have to be reassembled into a
wide vector via a chain of `shufflevector`s in the hot inner loop.

Example surfacing the cost: a 4096x4096 dynamic-shape bf16xbf16->f32
matmul with `--iree-llvmcpu-enable-inner-tiled` on Zen 4 lowered to
inner_tiled with N=16, K_inner=2. The RHS for one K-step is a
`vector<16x2xbf16>` from a contiguous 64-byte slice. Unrolling to 16
separate `<2 x bfloat>` loads forced a sequence of `vpermt2d`/
`vpermt2q` per K-iteration in the inner loop to rebuild the wide
RHS register — accounting for ~3 cycles of extra work per K-step on
top of the 29 dpbf16ps doing the real work.

Apply `populateFlattenVectorTransferPatterns` *before* the
rank-reduction patterns. It rewrites a multi-dim transfer with
contiguous trailing dims into a transfer on a `memref.collapse_shape`
view + a `vector.shape_cast`, so the read ends up as a single 1-D
transfer over the collapsed view and lowers to one wide `vector.load`.
Per-fragment effect on the matmul benchmark above: 80.8 ms -> 67.1 ms
(1.20x). Combined with the m_bcst-fold broadcast routing in a sibling
commit, end-to-end gets to 53.4 ms (within 5% of the precompiled
mmt4d ukernel at 50.9 ms).

Test fallout: two pipelines now lower a per-row pack-tile load into
a single wide load over a collapsed-memref view rather than one load
per row (`aligned_unpack_generic` in pipeline_pack_unpack_tests) /
write a constant `vector<4x2xi1>` mask as a single flat `vector<8xi1>`
store (`transpose_mask` in vector_lowering). The new IR is strictly
fewer ops in both cases; updated the CHECK lines to match.

Progress towards #24515.

Signed-off-by: Benoit Jacob <jacob.benoit.1@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Flatten contiguous trailing dims of transfers before unrolling.

`VectorTransferLoweringPass` applies the MLIR transfer-lowering patterns
with `maxTransferRank=1` plus full-unroll, which fully unrolls any
rank-N>1 `vector.transfer_read`/`transfer_write` to multiple rank-1
transfers (one per index of the outer dim). For multi-dim tiles whose
trailing dims are contiguous in memory, this unrolls a single wide
load into many narrow ones, which then have to be reassembled into a
wide vector via a chain of `shufflevector`s in the hot inner loop.

Example surfacing the cost: a 4096x4096 dynamic-shape bf16xbf16->f32
matmul with `--iree-llvmcpu-enable-inner-tiled` on Zen 4 lowered to
inner_tiled with N=16, K_inner=2. The RHS for one K-step is a
`vector<16x2xbf16>` from a contiguous 64-byte slice. Unrolling to 16
separate `<2 x bfloat>` loads forced a sequence of `vpermt2d`/
`vpermt2q` per K-iteration in the inner loop to rebuild the wide
RHS register — accounting for ~3 cycles of extra work per K-step on
top of the 29 dpbf16ps doing the real work.

Apply `populateFlattenVectorTransferPatterns` *before* the
rank-reduction patterns. It rewrites a multi-dim transfer with
contiguous trailing dims into a transfer on a `memref.collapse_shape`
view + a `vector.shape_cast`, so the read ends up as a single 1-D
transfer over the collapsed view and lowers to one wide `vector.load`.
Per-fragment effect on the matmul benchmark above: 80.8 ms -> 67.1 ms
(1.20x). Combined with the m_bcst-fold broadcast routing in a sibling
commit, end-to-end gets to 53.4 ms (within 5% of the precompiled
mmt4d ukernel at 50.9 ms).

Test fallout: two pipelines now lower a per-row pack-tile load into
a single wide load over a collapsed-memref view rather than one load
per row (`aligned_unpack_generic` in pipeline_pack_unpack_tests) /
write a constant `vector<4x2xi1>` mask as a single flat `vector<8xi1>`
store (`transpose_mask` in vector_lowering). The new IR is strictly
fewer ops in both cases; updated the CHECK lines to match.

Progress towards #24515.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Rework inner_tiled operand broadcast for m_bcst folding.

The CPU `inner_tiled` lowering replicates whichever of LHS/RHS has fewer
lanes up to the other's lane count before calling the LLVM intrinsic.
This reworks how that replication is emitted, for both performance and
correctness.

Previously the lowering emitted `vector.broadcast` to a `(replicate, K)`
2-D shape + `vector.shape_cast`, passed the broadcasted operand into the
LHS intrinsic slot, and -- for the `*_CASTF32` (f16->f32) and `*_CASTI16`
(i8->i16) variants -- widened the narrow operand to the intrinsic
element type *after* the broadcast.

Two problems:

1. The broadcast IR shape did not pattern-match LLVM's x86 `m_bcst`
   fold, so every `vdpbf16ps` was preceded by a separate `vbroadcastss`.
   ISel's `m_bcst` patterns key on the canonical `_mm512_set1_ps`-style
   splat (`insertelement ... 0` + `shufflevector ... zeroinitializer`),
   and the ISA-level broadcast EVEX operand is on the *third* source of
   dpbf16ps/vpdpwssd/pmaddwd.

2. Widening after the broadcast was both wasteful (the extend ran on the
   full replicated vector, once per unrolled M row) and, combined with
   the packed-lane splat idiom below, *miscompiled*: broadcast-then-widen
   forms `arith.extsi(vector.bitcast <N x i16> -> <2N x i8>)`, whose
   lowering drops the sign extension -- the i8 operand lanes come back
   zero-extended (a `vpand`/`vpsrlvw` mask-and-shift instead of
   `vpmovsxbw`). Negative i8 inputs then produce wrong matmul results.

Rework:
- Widen `*_CAST*` operands to the intrinsic element type *before*
  broadcasting, so the broadcast unit is already the intrinsic element
  type and no narrowing `vector.bitcast` feeds an `arith.extsi`.
- Emit the broadcast as the splat-of-a-single-packed-lane idiom: bitcast
  the source to a 1-lane vector of width `K * elem_bits`, extract the
  scalar, `vector.broadcast` to `replicate` lanes, bitcast back. This is
  the IR shape x86 ISel folds into the `m32bcst`/`m64bcst` EVEX
  broadcast operand.
- Route the broadcasted operand into the m_bcst-foldable slot for the
  symmetric intrinsics (third source of dpbf16ps/vpdpwssd/pmaddwd, `b`
  of FMA's `a*b+c`). vpdpbusd is asymmetric; its existing sign-aware
  routing already lands the broadcast in the foldable slot.

Measured on Zen 4 (4096x4096, dynamic shapes), inner_tiled:
  - bf16xbf16->f32: 80.8 ms -> 62.7 ms; all 29 `vdpbf16ps` now use the
    `{1to16}` memory-broadcast form (vs 0 before).
  - f16xf16->f32: 138 ms -> 126 ms (now faster than the mmt4d ukernel).
  - i8/i16/f32: essentially unchanged.

Progress towards #24515.

The CPU `inner_tiled` lowering replicates whichever of LHS/RHS has fewer
lanes up to the other's lane count before calling the LLVM intrinsic.
This reworks how that replication is emitted, for both performance and
correctness.

Previously the lowering emitted `vector.broadcast` to a `(replicate, K)`
2-D shape + `vector.shape_cast`, passed the broadcasted operand into the
LHS intrinsic slot, and -- for the `*_CASTF32` (f16->f32) and `*_CASTI16`
(i8->i16) variants -- widened the narrow operand to the intrinsic
element type *after* the broadcast.

Two problems:

1. The broadcast IR shape did not pattern-match LLVM's x86 `m_bcst`
   fold, so every `vdpbf16ps` was preceded by a separate `vbroadcastss`.
   ISel's `m_bcst` patterns key on the canonical `_mm512_set1_ps`-style
   splat (`insertelement ... 0` + `shufflevector ... zeroinitializer`),
   and the ISA-level broadcast EVEX operand is on the *third* source of
   dpbf16ps/vpdpwssd/pmaddwd.

2. Widening after the broadcast was both wasteful (the extend ran on the
   full replicated vector, once per unrolled M row) and, combined with
   the packed-lane splat idiom below, *miscompiled*: broadcast-then-widen
   forms `arith.extsi(vector.bitcast <N x i16> -> <2N x i8>)`, whose
   lowering drops the sign extension -- the i8 operand lanes come back
   zero-extended (a `vpand`/`vpsrlvw` mask-and-shift instead of
   `vpmovsxbw`). Negative i8 inputs then produce wrong matmul results.

Rework:
- Widen `*_CAST*` operands to the intrinsic element type *before*
  broadcasting, so the broadcast unit is already the intrinsic element
  type and no narrowing `vector.bitcast` feeds an `arith.extsi`.
- Emit the broadcast as the splat-of-a-single-packed-lane idiom: bitcast
  the source to a 1-lane vector of width `K * elem_bits`, extract the
  scalar, `vector.broadcast` to `replicate` lanes, bitcast back. This is
  the IR shape x86 ISel folds into the `m32bcst`/`m64bcst` EVEX
  broadcast operand.
- Route the broadcasted operand into the m_bcst-foldable slot for the
  symmetric intrinsics (third source of dpbf16ps/vpdpwssd/pmaddwd, `b`
  of FMA's `a*b+c`). vpdpbusd is asymmetric; its existing sign-aware
  routing already lands the broadcast in the foldable slot.

Measured on Zen 4 (4096x4096, dynamic shapes), inner_tiled:
  - bf16xbf16->f32: 80.8 ms -> 62.7 ms; all 29 `vdpbf16ps` now use the
    `{1to16}` memory-broadcast form (vs 0 before).
  - f16xf16->f32: 138 ms -> 126 ms (now faster than the mmt4d ukernel).
  - i8/i16/f32: essentially unchanged.

Progress towards #24515.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Flatten contiguous trailing dims of transfers before unrolling.

`VectorTransferLoweringPass` applies the MLIR transfer-lowering patterns
with `maxTransferRank=1` plus full-unroll, which fully unrolls any
rank-N>1 `vector.transfer_read`/`transfer_write` to multiple rank-1
transfers (one per index of the outer dim). For multi-dim tiles whose
trailing dims are contiguous in memory, this unrolls a single wide
load into many narrow ones, which then have to be reassembled into a
wide vector via a chain of `shufflevector`s in the hot inner loop.

Example surfacing the cost: a 4096x4096 dynamic-shape bf16xbf16->f32
matmul with `--iree-llvmcpu-enable-inner-tiled` on Zen 4 lowered to
inner_tiled with N=16, K_inner=2. The RHS for one K-step is a
`vector<16x2xbf16>` from a contiguous 64-byte slice. Unrolling to 16
separate `<2 x bfloat>` loads forced a sequence of `vpermt2d`/
`vpermt2q` per K-iteration in the inner loop to rebuild the wide
RHS register — accounting for ~3 cycles of extra work per K-step on
top of the 29 dpbf16ps doing the real work.

Apply `populateFlattenVectorTransferPatterns` *before* the
rank-reduction patterns. It rewrites a multi-dim transfer with
contiguous trailing dims into a transfer on a `memref.collapse_shape`
view + a `vector.shape_cast`, so the read ends up as a single 1-D
transfer over the collapsed view and lowers to one wide `vector.load`.
Per-fragment effect on the matmul benchmark above: 80.8 ms -> 67.1 ms
(1.20x). Combined with the m_bcst-fold broadcast routing in a sibling
commit, end-to-end gets to 53.4 ms (within 5% of the precompiled
mmt4d ukernel at 50.9 ms).

Test fallout: two pipelines now lower a per-row pack-tile load into
a single wide load over a collapsed-memref view rather than one load
per row (`aligned_unpack_generic` in pipeline_pack_unpack_tests) /
write a constant `vector<4x2xi1>` mask as a single flat `vector<8xi1>`
store (`transpose_mask` in vector_lowering). The new IR is strictly
fewer ops in both cases; updated the CHECK lines to match.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Rework inner_tiled operand broadcast for m_bcst folding.

The CPU `inner_tiled` lowering replicates whichever of LHS/RHS has fewer
lanes up to the other's lane count before calling the LLVM intrinsic.
This reworks how that replication is emitted, for both performance and
correctness.

Previously the lowering emitted `vector.broadcast` to a `(replicate, K)`
2-D shape + `vector.shape_cast`, passed the broadcasted operand into the
LHS intrinsic slot, and -- for the `*_CASTF32` (f16->f32) and `*_CASTI16`
(i8->i16) variants -- widened the narrow operand to the intrinsic
element type *after* the broadcast.

Two problems:

1. The broadcast IR shape did not pattern-match LLVM's x86 `m_bcst`
   fold, so every `vdpbf16ps` was preceded by a separate `vbroadcastss`.
   ISel's `m_bcst` patterns key on the canonical `_mm512_set1_ps`-style
   splat (`insertelement ... 0` + `shufflevector ... zeroinitializer`),
   and the ISA-level broadcast EVEX operand is on the *third* source of
   dpbf16ps/vpdpwssd/pmaddwd.

2. Widening after the broadcast was both wasteful (the extend ran on the
   full replicated vector, once per unrolled M row) and, combined with
   the packed-lane splat idiom below, *miscompiled*: broadcast-then-widen
   forms `arith.extsi(vector.bitcast <N x i16> -> <2N x i8>)`, whose
   lowering drops the sign extension -- the i8 operand lanes come back
   zero-extended (a `vpand`/`vpsrlvw` mask-and-shift instead of
   `vpmovsxbw`). Negative i8 inputs then produce wrong matmul results.

Rework:
- Widen `*_CAST*` operands to the intrinsic element type *before*
  broadcasting, so the broadcast unit is already the intrinsic element
  type and no narrowing `vector.bitcast` feeds an `arith.extsi`.
- Emit the broadcast as the splat-of-a-single-packed-lane idiom: bitcast
  the source to a 1-lane vector of width `K * elem_bits`, extract the
  scalar, `vector.broadcast` to `replicate` lanes, bitcast back. This is
  the IR shape x86 ISel folds into the `m32bcst`/`m64bcst` EVEX
  broadcast operand.
- Route the broadcasted operand into the m_bcst-foldable slot for the
  symmetric intrinsics (third source of dpbf16ps/vpdpwssd/pmaddwd, `b`
  of FMA's `a*b+c`). vpdpbusd is asymmetric; its existing sign-aware
  routing already lands the broadcast in the foldable slot.

Measured on Zen 4 (4096x4096, dynamic shapes), inner_tiled:
  - bf16xbf16->f32: 80.8 ms -> 62.7 ms; all 29 `vdpbf16ps` now use the
    `{1to16}` memory-broadcast form (vs 0 before).
  - f16xf16->f32: 138 ms -> 126 ms (now faster than the mmt4d ukernel).
  - i8/i16/f32: essentially unchanged.

Progress towards #24515.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Flatten contiguous trailing dims of transfers before unrolling.

`VectorTransferLoweringPass` applies the MLIR transfer-lowering patterns
with `maxTransferRank=1` plus full-unroll, which fully unrolls any
rank-N>1 `vector.transfer_read`/`transfer_write` to multiple rank-1
transfers (one per index of the outer dim). For multi-dim tiles whose
trailing dim is a tiny contiguous chunk, this unrolls a single wide
load into many narrow ones, which then have to be reassembled into a
wide vector via a chain of `shufflevector`s in the hot inner loop.

Example surfacing the cost: a 4096x4096 dynamic-shape bf16xbf16->f32
matmul with `--iree-llvmcpu-enable-inner-tiled` on Zen 4 lowered to
inner_tiled with N=16, K_inner=2. The RHS for one K-step is a
`vector<16x2xbf16>` from a contiguous 64-byte slice. Unrolling to 16
separate `<2 x bfloat>` loads forced a sequence of `vpermt2d`/
`vpermt2q` per K-iteration in the inner loop to rebuild the wide
RHS register — accounting for ~3 cycles of extra work per K-step on
top of the 29 dpbf16ps doing the real work.

Apply `populateFlattenVectorTransferPatterns` *before* the
rank-reduction patterns. It rewrites a multi-dim transfer with
contiguous trailing dims into a transfer on a `memref.collapse_shape`
view + a `vector.shape_cast`, so the read ends up as a single 1-D
transfer over the collapsed view and lowers to one wide `vector.load`.
Per-fragment effect on the matmul benchmark above: 80.8 ms -> 67.1 ms
(1.20x). Combined with the m_bcst-fold broadcast routing in a sibling
commit, end-to-end gets to 53.4 ms (within 5% of the precompiled
mmt4d ukernel at 50.9 ms).

Gate the flattening on the trailing-dim bitwidth, passing
`targetVectorBitwidth = 64`: only flatten transfers whose innermost dim
is a sub-64-bit chunk. A transfer whose innermost dim is already a
register-fraction-sized chunk (`<4xf32>`, `<8xf32>`, `<16xf32>`, ...)
tiles fine via plain rank reduction; flattening *that* would fuse the
rows into one oversized 1-D transfer and then re-split it with a
`vector.shape_cast` (a chain of extracts), inflating generated code
size with no benefit and regressing whole-model .vmfb size. The packed
inner-tile K dimensions that motivate this change are all <= 32 bits,
so they are still flattened.

Test fallout: `transpose_mask` in vector_lowering now writes a constant
`vector<4x2xi1>` mask (trailing dim 2 bits) as a single flat
`vector<8xi1>` store rather than per-row; strictly fewer ops, updated
the CHECK lines to match.

Progress towards #24515.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Benoit Jacob <jacob.benoit.1@gmail.com>
